response.answer: Adopt the Delphi method with diverse stakeholders and set a 75% consensus threshold. Pre-list validated instruments like the EPA's Health Effects Inventory for PFAS.

results.title: PFAS National Primary Drinking Water Regulation Rulemaking
results.content: As a result, EPA is proposing to use a Hazard Index (HI) approach to protecting public health from mixtures of four PFAS: PFHxS, HFPO-DA and its ammonium salt (also known as GenX chemicals), PFNA, and PFBS because of their known and additive toxic effects and occurrence and likely co-occurrence in drinking water. EPA found that PFOA and PFOS may have an adverse effect on the health of persons; that these contaminants are known to occur, or that there is a substantial likelihood that they will occur, in PWSs with a frequency and at levels that present a public health concern; and that regulation of PFOA and PFOS presents a meaningful opportunity for health risk reduction for persons served by PWSs. As discussed in the final Regulatory Determinations 4 Notice for CCL 4 contaminants (USEPA, 2021d) and EPA's PFAS Strategic Roadmap (USEPA, 2022c), the Agency has also evaluated additional PFAS chemicals for regulatory consideration as supported by the best available science.
